scheme_name: Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation
description:
The Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to enhance coffee production in traditional coffee-growing regions.

This scheme was officially launched on 1st April 2021 as part of the larger National Coffee Policy.

The primary objective of this scheme is to improve the water supply for coffee cultivation in traditional coffee-growing areas.

The scheme aims to increase coffee productivity by ensuring that coffee plants receive adequate water throughout the year.

One of the measurable targets of this scheme is to increase the average yield of coffee from 1,000 kg per hectare to 1,500 kg per hectare by the year 2025.

The scheme also aims to enhance the income of coffee growers by at least 20 percent within the next five years.

The benefits of the scheme include the provision of financial assistance for the installation of water harvesting structures.

Under this scheme, farmers can receive up to ₹1 lakh for constructing rainwater harvesting systems.

The financial assistance is provided at a subsidy rate of 50 percent for small and marginal farmers.

For larger farmers, the subsidy rate is set at 30 percent.

The scheme also includes the provision of drip irrigation systems to ensure efficient water usage.

Farmers can receive financial assistance of up to ₹2 lakh for the installation of drip irrigation systems.

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are specific and well-defined.

Farmers must be engaged in coffee cultivation in traditional coffee-growing areas to qualify for the benefits.

The definition of traditional coffee-growing areas includes regions in Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.

Farmers must also possess land ownership documents to apply for the scheme.

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years.

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for this scheme.

The application process is straightforward and involves several steps.

Interested farmers must first visit the official website of the Coffee Board of India.

They need to download the application form available on the website.

The completed application form must be submitted to the nearest Coffee Board office along with the required documents.

Required documents include land ownership proof, identity proof, and a bank account statement.

Farmers must also submit a project report detailing the proposed water augmentation measures.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by officials from the Coffee Board.

The approval process typically takes about 30 days from the date of submission.

Upon approval, the financial assistance will be disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account.

The disbursement of funds is done in two installments.

The first installment is released after the approval of the project.

The second installment is released after the successful implementation of the water augmentation measures.

The scheme is implemented by the Coffee Board of India under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

The Coffee Board has regional offices in major coffee-growing states to facilitate the implementation of the scheme.

Farmers can contact the Coffee Board's helpline for any queries related to the scheme.

The helpline number is 1800 425 1111.

The scheme is expected to benefit over 50,000 coffee farmers across the traditional coffee-growing regions.

The total budget allocated for the scheme is ₹200 crore for the first three years.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote sustainable agriculture practices in India.

It aligns with the Government of India's goal to double farmers' income by 2022.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of water conservation in agriculture.

Farmers are encouraged to adopt modern irrigation techniques to maximize water efficiency.

The implementation of this scheme is expected to contribute to the overall growth of the coffee sector in India.

India is currently the seventh-largest producer of coffee in the world.

The country produces approximately 3 lakh metric tons of coffee annually.

Karnataka alone accounts for about 70 percent of the total coffee production in India.

The coffee sector provides employment to over 2.5 million people in the country.

The Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation scheme is a significant step towards enhancing the livelihoods of coffee farmers.

It aims to address the challenges posed by climate change and water scarcity.

Farmers are encouraged to adopt rainwater harvesting techniques to ensure water availability.

The scheme also promotes the use of organic farming practices among coffee growers.

Training programs are organized by the Coffee Board to educate farmers about sustainable practices.

The Coffee Board collaborates with various agricultural universities to provide technical support.

The scheme is expected to have a positive impact on the quality of coffee produced in India.

Higher quality coffee is likely to fetch better prices in the domestic and international markets.

The scheme also aims to promote the export of Indian coffee by improving its quality.

Farmers are encouraged to form cooperatives to enhance bargaining power and access to markets.

The Coffee Board provides assistance in marketing coffee through various channels.

The implementation of this scheme is monitored through regular assessments and feedback from farmers.

The Coffee Board conducts annual reviews to evaluate the impact of the scheme on coffee production.

The scheme is expected to create a ripple effect in rural economies by increasing income levels.

It aims to empower farmers by providing them with the necessary resources for sustainable farming.

The Development Support for Coffee in Traditional Areas: Water Augmentation scheme is a crucial initiative for the future of coffee cultivation in India.
